title: Windows Job Object provider process boundary
description: Objective: provide the real per-run Windows process primitive required by the Claude launcher. Deliverable: an internal @moe/runner Node/Windows binding that creates the provider child suspended, attaches it to a dedicated Job Object configured with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and no breakaway, then resumes it; exposes shell-free argv launch, bounded cwd/environment/stdio, proven process identity, awaited exit, terminate, and handle closure. A taskkill-only implementation is not sufficient because it cannot prove descendants dead after the root exits. NOT in scope: Claude runtime discovery/pinning, activation grants, daemon/store orchestration, evidence receipts, or public @moe/runner launcher export. Real consumer: Windows Claude launch wrapper task task-acf73253a204435aba590894799814f2. Owned paths: a focused packages/runner/src/platform/windows/** binding/test seam plus the minimal runner manifest/lockfile/native-build paths selected during planning. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test plus a Windows parent+grandchild termination smoke.
definitionOfDone: On Windows, the provider process is created suspended and cannot execute before a dedicated Job Object is created, configured kill-on-close without breakaway, and successfully receives the child; only then is the child resumed.

Every create/configure/assign/resume/query/terminate/close failure returns an immutable UNKNOWN result with an exact stable PROCESS_BOUNDARY code and refusing layer; partial children are terminated and every native/process/stream handle is awaited and closed.

Launch accepts an executable plus argv array with shell disabled and validates a bounded absolute cwd and allowlisted bounded environment; malformed, oversized, UNC/device, or unverifiable inputs produce exact refusal codes before process creation.

Closing/cancelling/timing out the boundary kills the controlled parent and a deliberately detached grandchild; tests prove both PIDs terminate and assert a positive generated case count plus the exact code/layer for every refusal arm.

Non-Windows import is safe and invocation returns typed UNSUPPORTED with zero native/process calls; the chosen native dependency/helper is version-pinned and runtime-loadable on the supported Windows Node version.
The focused runner gates and a foreground Windows process-tree smoke exit 0, with no generated addon/build/debug artifacts committed.
taskRails: Use Microsoft Job Object semantics; taskkill-only or PID-enumeration-only cleanup cannot satisfy proven whole-tree termination.
TDD; failure tests assert exact stable code and layer and zero process execution where refusal precedes creation.
Keep every production source focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
This is an internal process boundary. Do not add daemon/store authority or claim durable activation-grant consumption.

PROTOCOL CONSTANTS MIRRORED (read from source, not prose):
- PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1 (protocol.rs:32). FRAME_HEADER_BYTES = 6 (frames.rs:43).
- Header (frames.rs:13-16): off0 u8 version | off1 u8 opcode | off2 u32 LITTLE-ENDIAN declared length | off6 payload.
- Caps: MAX_CONTROL_PAYLOAD 64*1024, MAX_STATUS_PAYLOAD 4*1024, MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_PAYLOAD 512.
- Inbound (control.rs): Launch=1, Cancel=2. Outbound (status.rs): Started=1, Completed=2, Refused=3.
- Started payload 12B: pid u32 LE + creation_time u64 LE. Completed payload 5B: kind u8 (1 Exited / 2 Unknown) + u32 LE; unknown wire NotWaited=1 StillRunning=2 WaitAbandoned=3 ProofFromAnotherProcess=4.
- Refused payload 7B (REFUSED_PAYLOAD_BYTES): layer u8 + reason u16 LE + code u32 LE. RefusalLayer wire 1-based: Descriptor=1, Protocol=2, Native=3.
- ProtocolReason::ALL 10 in order: VersionMismatch LengthOverLimit FrameTruncated ChannelFailed UnknownOpcode PayloadMalformed TrailingBytes DuplicateLaunch FrameOutOfOrder FrameAfterTerminal. ProtocolStage::ALL 2: Framing, Control (Framing owns the first four).
- Launch payload order (control.rs decode_launch): text(executable) list(argv) text(cwd) pairs(environment); text = u16 LE byte length + UTF-8; list = u16 LE count + texts; pairs = u16 LE count + (text,text)*.

VOCABULARIES, closed and frozen, following platform-contract.ts style:
- WINDOWS_PROCESS_TRUTH_CLASSES = ["PROVEN","UNKNOWN"] — UNKNOWN is the floor.
- WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS, 6 members. Three on THIS side (WINDOWS_PROCESS_REQUEST / _RESOLUTION / _TRANSPORT) and three MIRRORING the broker's RefusalLayer (BROKER_DESCRIPTOR / BROKER_PROTOCOL / BROKER_NATIVE), so a refusal that crossed the wire keeps its layer identity rather than flattening to "the boundary refused". A check migrating between TypeScript and the broker now has to move a test's expected layer.
- WINDOWS_PROCESS_CODES, 22 members, hand-written, no catch-all.

ONE DELIBERATE DESIGN CALL WORTH REVIEW: there is a SINGLE code (PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED) for all three broker layers, not three, and no TS re-spelling of the broker's ProtocolReason/DescriptorReason/NativeOp vocabularies. Re-spelling them would duplicate authority that already has a frozen definition and one owner. Exactness is preserved by the triple (code, layer, brokerReason.reason): brokerReason carries the LAYER-LOCAL ordinal plus the Win32 code, which is exactly what refusal.rs puts on the wire. DoD 2's create/configure/assign/resume/query/terminate/close set arrives as layer BROKER_NATIVE with reason = position in NativeOp::ALL (19 ops, win32.rs:33-53), so each of those operations is still identified exactly.

IMMUTABILITY, by construction not by convention:
- provenRun() is the ONLY constructor of a PROVEN outcome and it REFUSES rather than trusts: a zero/negative/fractional pid, a zero creation time, or a non-integer/negative exit all come back as UNKNOWN with PROCESS_BOUNDARY_IDENTITY_UNPROVEN on WINDOWS_PROCESS_TRANSPORT. So "a PROVEN result always carries a full pid+creationTime pair" holds by construction. A PID-only proof is unrepresentable — the shape DoD 4 forbids.
- creationTime is a bigint, not a number: a FILETIME (134309515541692727 measured on this host) is past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and would silently lose its low digits as a double, which is exactly how a reused-PID check goes vacuous.
- unknownOutcome() COPIES the caller's brokerReason/identity rather than freezing them in place. Freezing in place would reach out and mutate an object this module does not own; not copying would leave the caller's retained reference a back door that can rewrite a recorded refusal. Both directions are asserted.
- brokerLayerFromWire is 1-BASED, pinned by value against RefusalLayer::wire, and the closed-set test sweeps all 256 bytes asserting exactly 253 answer null (positive generated-case count asserted, so a sweep producing zero cases fails).

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: THE FRAME CODEC TESTS, WITH BYTE-EXACT FIXTURES. Write these before the codec exists. The TS side necessarily re-implements the 6-byte header -- that is a duplicated FORMAT, not duplicated authority, and it is the one place a second implementation is legitimate. It is also where silent drift happens, so pin it against the RUST CONSTANTS, not against the doc comment: version at offset 0, opcode at offset 1, LITTLE-ENDIAN u32 declared length at offset 2, payload at offset 6. Cover: a wrong version byte refuses with its exact reason; a declared length near u32::MAX is refused BEFORE any allocation or subarray to that size; a truncated header and a truncated payload each refuse distinctly; and -- the case synthetic tests usually miss -- CHUNK BOUNDARIES, since a pipe delivers partial frames and several frames in one chunk. Feed the same bytes fragmented one-byte-at-a-time and fully coalesced and assert identical results. A reader that assumes one chunk equals one frame passes every naive test and fails against the real broker.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `npx vitest run --root . packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-frames.test.ts` exits 1: "Error: Cannot find module './windows-frames.js'". The codec does not exist; the tests were written first.

windows-frames.test.ts covers, in four groups:

1. THE ANTI-DRIFT PIN AGAINST THE RUST SOURCE (not against its doc comment). The test READS native/broker/src/{protocol,frames}.rs and compares: PROTOCOL_VERSION parsed out of `pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: u8 = 1;`, FRAME_HEADER_BYTES, and all three caps (MAX_CONTROL_PAYLOAD / MAX_STATUS_PAYLOAD / MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_PAYLOAD, with a tiny `N` / `N * M` evaluator since Rust spells them `64 * 1024`). It also asserts FRAME_HEADER_BYTES === 1+1+4 so a header that grows breaks the sum, and asserts the three caps are DISTINCT so one global number cannot be substituted. ENDIANNESS is pinned by reading the CALLS: frames.rs must contain `u32::from_le_bytes` and must NOT contain `from_be_bytes` or `to_be_bytes`, so a Rust flip to big-endian reddens here before production disagrees. Every extractor throws by name if its declaration moves, so a silently-zero pin is impossible.

2. BYTE-EXACT ENCODER FIXTURES, literal bytes so a wrong offset is a value mismatch. Empty CANCEL is exactly [01 02 00 00 00 00]. The LE pin uses payload length 258 = 0x00000102, whose LE header bytes [01 01 02 01 00 00] share NO byte position with the BE spelling [01 01 00 00 01 02] — so the fixture cannot pass under writeUInt32BE (this is the step-9 drill target). Version-at-0 / opcode-at-1 asserted separately so a swap is caught. Over-cap encode refuses with PROCESS_BOUNDARY_FRAME_OVERSIZED on WINDOWS_PROCESS_TRANSPORT; exactly-at-cap is accepted, so the bound is pinned inclusive on both sides.

3. HOSTILE HEADERS. Wrong version -> exact FRAME_VERSION_MISMATCH + layer. ORDER IS THE CONTRACT and mirrors read_frame (frames.rs:129-146): a frame that is BOTH wrong-version and 0xFFFFFFFF-long must answer VERSION_MISMATCH, not OVERSIZED — a bound-check-first reader would make a future protocol re-layout read as garbage. The near-u32::MAX case (0xFFFFFFFF = 4 GiB) asserts REFUSED **rather than PENDING**, which is the discriminating assertion: a reader that waits for `6 + declared` bytes before bound-checking answers PENDING forever and one that sizes a buffer first throws — and it asserts buffered() === 6, so nothing past the header was ever touched. Per-channel cap tested by having the SAME bytes refuse on DIAGNOSTIC and be PENDING on CONTROL. A one-byte push answers PENDING, pinning that the whole header is read before the version is judged (the Rust order).

4. CHUNK BOUNDARIES — the case synthetic tests miss, since fd1 delivers partial frames and several frames per chunk. A three-frame stream is read identically when (a) fully coalesced into one chunk, (b) fragmented one byte at a time, and (c) split at 3/5/7/... sizes deliberately coprime with the 6-byte header so splits land inside a header, inside a length field and inside a payload. A hostile trailing frame must refuse at the SAME point with the SAME code under both coalesced and fragmented delivery. Plus a nesting case: an outer frame whose payload IS a well-formed frame must yield ONE read, so a reader that rescans its own buffer instead of consuming exactly the declared length is caught. Frame counts are asserted exactly (3, 1, 2) so a run producing zero frames cannot pass.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN: THE TS FRAME CODEC. Create packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-frames.ts and its .js bridge. Implement the reader/writer over a chunk-accumulating buffer. NEVER allocate or slice to a declared length before bounds-checking it against the cap -- frames.rs:22-31 documents exactly why the Rust side checks first, and the TS side faces the same hostile input. Keep this module bytes-only, as its Rust counterpart is: it knows version, declared length and payload extent, and interprets no opcode. Under 250 physical lines.

GREEN. packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-frames.ts, 233 physical lines (grep -c ''), under the 250 cap, plus its exact one-line .js bridge. `npx vitest run --root . packages/runner/src/platform/windows` -> 2 files / 37 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` -> exit 0.

BYTES ONLY, like its Rust counterpart: the module knows version, declared length and payload extent and interprets NO opcode, so one codec serves fd0/fd1/fd2 without embedding three vocabularies.

THE THREE THINGS THAT MAKE IT NOT-NAIVE:

1. THE BOUND CHECK PRECEDES EVERYTHING SIZED FROM THE DECLARATION. next() reads the header, checks the version, then compares `declared > cap` against a compile-time constant, and only then computes `FRAME_HEADER_BYTES + declared` or touches the buffer. Checking availability first would turn a 4 GiB declaration into an unbounded wait rather than a refusal — that is the exact inversion step 9 drills.

2. readDeclaredLength USES `* 0x1000000`, NOT `<< 24`. This is a real trap, not defensive decoration: under JavaScript's SIGNED 32-bit bitwise operators, `head[5] << 24` for a top byte >= 0x80 is NEGATIVE, so a length near u32::MAX would compute as negative, compare as LESS than the cap, and sail straight through the bound check immediately above its only caller. Multiplying keeps it unsigned. The 0xFFFFFFFF test is what holds this.

3. THE READER IS CHUNK-AGNOSTIC. push() only appends; next() drains and consumes exactly `6 + declared`. A refusal LATCHES — a refused channel stays refused, because resuming after a hostile frame would let a peer resynchronise the stream on bytes of its own choosing. Payloads are taken with `slice`, not `subarray`: a view would alias and retain the whole accumulated buffer this reader is about to drop.

ORDER MIRRORS read_frame (frames.rs:129-146) exactly: whole header, then VERSION, then the bound check, then the payload. Encoding writes the little-endian length as four explicit byte stores rather than a DataView call, so the layout the Rust side pins is literally the four lines of code.

TRUNCATION IS ONLY KNOWABLE AT finish(). Before the channel ends, "short" and "slow" are indistinguishable, so a partial frame is PENDING and never an error. finish() then distinguishes a truncated HEADER from a truncated PAYLOAD via two exported message constants — separate because only the second implicates the peer (it promised bytes it never sent) — and the tests assert the exported symbols rather than retyped strings.

encodeFrame refuses its own over-cap payload (PROCESS_BOUNDARY_FRAME_OVERSIZED) and a non-byte opcode (PROCESS_BOUNDARY_FRAME_OPCODE_UNKNOWN) instead of emitting a frame the broker would have to defend against.

One test fix during GREEN: windows-frames.test.ts:27 needed `match?.[1]` hoisted into a checked local for noUncheckedIndexedAccess. No assertion changed.

implementationPlan.description: THE BOUNDARY: SPAWN THE BROKER AND DRIVE THE PROTOCOL. Create packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-boundary.ts and its .js bridge, following linux-boundary.ts as the structural precedent. It resolves the built broker binary deterministically, spawns it with `shell:false` and EXACTLY SIX pipes (fd0 control in, fd1 status out, fd2 bounded diagnostics, fd3/4/5 provider stdio), sends one launch request, and translates Started/Completed/Refused into the PROVEN/UNKNOWN vocabulary from step 2. DoD 3: accept an executable plus an argv ARRAY with shell disabled, and validate a bounded absolute cwd and an allowlisted bounded environment -- malformed, oversized, UNC or device paths refuse BEFORE the broker is spawned, and the test asserts no process was created rather than only that an error came back. DoD 5's runtime-loadability: if the broker binary cannot be resolved, return a typed UNKNOWN with its own stable code -- FAIL, never silently degrade to a shell or taskkill fallback. Under 250 lines; split resolution from protocol driving if it grows.

REFUSAL SWEEP AND THE NON-WINDOWS PATH. Extend the boundary tests to cover DoD 2 and DoD 5. Every create/configure/assign/resume/query/terminate/close failure surfaces an IMMUTABLE UNKNOWN carrying the exact stable code AND the refusing layer -- and where both the TS boundary and the broker could refuse the same input, the test pins WHICH one answered, or the assertion is one layer away from vacuous. Assert a nonzero exact generated-case count so a sweep producing zero cases fails. For DoD 5, prove the non-Windows path returns typed UNSUPPORTED with ZERO native or process calls -- prove it by injecting a spawn seam that records calls and asserting the log is EMPTY, not by reading the source. Follow the runner's existing platform pattern of returning a classification envelope rather than throwing.

THE FOREGROUND WINDOWS PROCESS-TREE SMOKE (DoD 4 and DoD 6). This runs for real on this win32 host -- no skip, no cfg gate; if it cannot locate the release broker it FAILS rather than passing vacuously. WHAT IT MUST AND MUST NOT PROVE: Job Object semantics and the detached-grandchild kill are ALREADY PROVEN in Rust by broker/tests/containment.rs (1085 lines) with broker/src/bin/detached_spawner.rs. Do not re-prove them. Prove THE FACADE DRIVES THEM: launch a provider that spawns a deliberately detached grandchild, then close/cancel/time out THROUGH THE TYPESCRIPT BOUNDARY, and assert both the parent and the grandchild are dead. Prove death by PID PLUS CREATION TIME for each -- Windows reuses PIDs, so a PID-only check can report an unrelated live process as the dead one. Assert a positive generated case count. Clean up every child and handle on every exit path INCLUDING failure; a stranded broker holds pipes open and flakes the next run.

WIRE UP, RESOLVE THE BINARY, AUDIT SIZE. Ensure the new modules are reachable however the runner's platform modules are (match how linux-boundary is surfaced; do NOT add a public @moe/runner launcher export -- the description's NOT-in-scope list forbids it). planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
COMPOSE THE BROKER, DO NOT REBUILD IT. Rejected implementing Job Object control in Node via a native addon or child_process+taskkill. The description's own rail 1 says taskkill-only cannot prove whole-tree termination, and the broker already proves it on a real kernel. Node's job is to spawn the broker with six pipes, speak the frame protocol, and translate outcomes into the runner's PROVEN/UNKNOWN vocabulary.

WHERE THE NATIVE DEPENDENCY LIVES (DoD 5's 'version-pinned and runtime-loadable'). The 'native dependency' is the broker BINARY produced by the pinned Rust toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.96.0, Cargo.lock is committed, windows-sys is exact-pinned =0.61.2). So version-pinning is already satisfied upstream; what this task must add is deterministic RESOLUTION of the built binary plus a runtime-loadability check that FAILS rather than silently degrades when it is missing. Do not vendor a prebuilt binary into the repo -- rail 3 and the epic forbid committing build artifacts.

FRAME CODEC: MIRROR, DO NOT SHARE. There is no way to share the Rust codec with TypeScript, so the TS side necessarily re-encodes the same 6-byte header. That is a duplicated FORMAT, not duplicated authority, and it is unavoidable -- but it must be pinned against the Rust definition by byte-exact fixtures rather than by reading the doc comment, or the two drift silently. This is the one place where a second implementation is legitimate, and it is why DoD 4 wants generated cases.

NON-WINDOWS PATH: TYPED UNSUPPORTED WITH ZERO PROCESS CALLS (DoD 5). Follow the runner's existing platform pattern -- a pure classification returning an UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED envelope -- rather than a thrown error, and prove zero native/process calls by injection rather than by inspection.

SCOPE BOUNDARY I AM DRAWING EXPLICITLY: this lands the internal boundary only. The description's own NOT-in-scope list excludes Claude discovery/pinning, activation grants, daemon/store orchestration, evidence receipts and any public @moe/runner launcher export. The real consumer is task-acf73253 (Windows Claude launch wrapper), which is BLOCKED on this task -- record it as the consumer edge per the pure-package clause.

THE WIRE FORMAT THE TS SIDE MUST MIRROR BYTE-FOR-BYTE, documented at broker/src/frames.rs:13-16 and pinned by FRAME_HEADER_BYTES = 6:

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE BIGGEST RISK IS SCOPE INVERSION -- a worker reading the description without reading the native tree will start writing a Node Job-Object binding and duplicate four completed tasks. Step 1 exists to stop that. If the broker tree is absent or its protocol has moved, STOP rather than improvising a Node implementation.

2. THE DECLARED LENGTH IS ATTACKER INPUT ON THE TS SIDE TOO. frames.rs:22-31 documents that the Rust reader bound-checks BEFORE committing to the declared size. The TS reader must do the same: never allocate or `subarray` to a declared length before comparing it against the cap, and never trust that the broker is the only thing that could ever write to fd1.

3. LITTLE-ENDIAN, AND THE HEADER IS 6 BYTES, NOT 8. `readUInt32LE(2)` with a 6-byte header is easy to write as `readUInt32BE` or to mis-offset. Pin it with byte-exact fixtures taken from the Rust constants, not from prose.

4. PIPE READS ARE CHUNKED. fd1 will deliver partial frames and multiple frames in one chunk. A reader that assumes one chunk equals one frame passes every unit test with synthetic input and fails against the real broker. Test with deliberately fragmented and coalesced chunk boundaries.

5. DoD 4 (parent + detached grandchild) IS ALREADY PROVEN IN RUST by broker/tests/containment.rs (1085 lines) and broker/src/bin/detached_spawner.rs. The Node smoke must prove THE FACADE DRIVES IT -- that closing/cancelling/timing out through the TS boundary results in both PIDs dead -- not re-prove Job Object semantics. Assert death by PID plus creation time, never PID alone; Windows reuses PIDs.

6. The smoke spawns real processes. Every handle and child must be cleaned up on every exit path including test failure, or a stranded broker holds pipes open and the next run flakes.

7. platform-contract.ts is AT 250 lines. If the design needs a PLATFORM_WINDOWS layer member there, that file is both at the cap and outside the owned paths. Raise it as a scope question explicitly rather than editing it quietly.
